name: Alpha Centauri B
notes: Position from the J2000 component direction and the 750.81 mas Alpha Centauri AB parallax from Akeson et al. (2021). Motion: Akeson et al. (2021) Alpha Centauri AB barycenter solution at J2019.5, shared by A and B; no binary orbital motion. Alpha Centauri B reviewed physical parameters. Akeson et al. (2021) combine the revised orbital parallax with published angular diameter and bolometric flux measurements for the mass, radius, and luminosity. Kervella et al. (2017) derive the effective temperature from interferometry and bolometric flux. Morel (2018) measures [Fe/H] in a differential HARPS abundance analysis. Joyce & Chaboyer (2018) infer the shared system age from classical and asteroseismic constraints. Reviewed companion expansion of bright-stars: Alpha Centauri B; adopted nearest-1000:alpha-centauri-b.

name: Sirius A
notes: Sirius system position and physical properties use Bond et al. (2017), including the adopted 378.9 mas parallax. The component offset is below this catalog's spatial precision. Motion: system motion shared by A and B; Hipparcos proper motion (SIMBAD HIP 32349; 2007A&A...474..653V) and true systemic RV -8.47 km/s from Bond et al. (2017) section V.1. No binary orbital motion; Galactic conversion documented in README. Sirius A reviewed physical parameters from Bond et al. (2017). The radius is interferometric, the mass dynamical, and the luminosity and temperature use the adopted parallax. The age and bulk [Fe/H] are stellar-evolution model results; the bulk metallicity is used instead of Sirius A's diffusion-altered Am photospheric abundance.

name: Sirius B
notes: Sirius system position and white-dwarf properties use Bond et al. (2017). The component offset is below this catalog's spatial precision. Motion: inherited Sirius system motion as for A; Hipparcos proper motion (2007A&A...474..653V) and true systemic RV -8.47 km/s from Bond et al. (2017) section V.1. Not the white dwarf's gravitationally redshifted RV; no binary orbital motion. Sirius B reviewed physical parameters from Bond et al. (2017). The mass is dynamical; temperature, radius, and luminosity come from HST/STIS atmosphere and absolute-flux fitting. The displayed age is the total evolutionary age, not merely the 126 Myr white-dwarf cooling time. Photospheric metallicity remains intentionally blank for this pure-hydrogen white dwarf. Reviewed companion expansion of bright-stars: Sirius B; adopted nearest-1000:sirius-b.

name: Procyon B
notes: 10pc census (2023-08-25), object 32, system 16; alf CMi B. J2000 Sun-relative Galactic position via Astropy; transverse-only; unknown/withheld RV, no exported velocity.   No orbital model. Procyon B component parameters from Bond et al. (2015), using the Provencal et al. (2002) HST atmosphere temperature and parallax-adjusted radius. Metal pollution is not represented as an ordinary stellar [Fe/H]. Cooling age 1.37 +/- 0.04 Gyr is retained here separately from the preferred total binary age of 2.70 Gyr; the displayed age is the latter and inherits the primary stellar-evolution assumptions. Component-resolved Johnson V=10.82 from 2002ApJ...568..324P; 2015ApJ...813..106B; absolute V uses the adopted distance. luminosity_solar derived by Stefan-Boltzmann scaling from adopted inputs (solar Teff=5772 K); inherits their measurement/model/estimate assumptions. Reviewed companion expansion of bright-stars: Procyon B; adopted nearest-1000:10pc-0032.
